agentResult.finalText:
Everything works now: the quick suite passes, the sealed `checks/contract.cjs` passes (it previously failed on the very first tenant-isolation assertion), and the new extended test file passes.

## What I changed

**`src/storage.js`** — `key` was `(tenant, id) => id`, discarding the tenant entirely, so identical ids in different tenants collided. It now returns `JSON.stringify([tenant, id])`, an injective encoding of the pair, so keys never collide even when tenant or id contain `|`, quoting, or other punctuation.

**`src/replay.js`** — replay filtered to `op === 'put'`, so `open(exportJournal())` silently lost all deletions. It now applies every event in order.

**`src/api.js`** — two fixes:
- `batch` bypassed `apply`: it always did `rows.set(k, e.value)`, so a `{op:'delete'}` event in a batch didn't delete, and it never invalidated the cache. It now routes each event through `mutate`, giving correct op handling, cache invalidation, journal append, and call-order semantics for free.
- `get`'s cache stored hits and misses but was never invalidated, so reads went stale after any mutation. `apply` now deletes the affected key from the cache, covering every mutation path (`put`, `remove`, `batch`, and replay itself).

**`tests/contract-full.test.cjs`** (new) — extended tests, one section per contract clause: fresh reads after every mutation path for both cached hits and misses, delimiter/collision and tenant-swap isolation, within-batch call order (including delete-then-put), full journal detachment (tampering with an export or with caller-held batch events must not affect state or later exports), replay fidelity with repeated replays, history preservation in reopened ledgers, and no by-reference retention of the `history` argument. I deliberately left `checks/contract.cjs` and `amabie.project.json` untouched so the sealed check stays intact.
